_comment: The bootstrap instance. It declares two directories — `skills/` and `workflows/` — because discovery reads declarations rather than walking the tree, and an undeclared directory is not this instance's graph however many files sit in it. TWO processes live here and exactly one of them is an ENTRY POINT: `workflows/initialize-harness.bpmn`. An Initiator that has read README.md is at its start event with nowhere else to begin. `workflows/log-message.bpmn` is the other, and it is an independent SUB-PROCESS — reached only by a callActivity from a step, never started — so it does not compete with the first for being the thing you begin. The constraint was never 'one file'; it is that there is one place to start. Cat-harness is composed ON TOP of this rather than being its parent, which is why nothing here may import from it.

assets.description: Phase one of two. Valid with nothing installed: no skills, no knowledge graph, no MCP, no beans. The default behaviour of initialisation is to copy this file, and the last bootstrap step re-enters through the installed harness, which is what supplies phase two. No `source` because this is the origin — an absent source means authored here, which is a different fact from an upstream that cannot be reached.

_directories_comment: ONE entry, and it is a subdirectory rather than `bootstrap/` itself. `isSkillMd` is declaration-over-location: a markdown file that does NOT declare `$schema:` is a skill. README.md and AGENTS.md declare neither, so a graph rooted at `bootstrap/` would count this instance's two DECLARED ASSETS as skill nodes — the instance has already said what those files are, and a scan would contradict its own declaration. Keeping the graph one level down means the two mechanisms cannot collide. Declared explicitly rather than relying on DEFAULT_DIRECTORIES: a declaration that exists is honoured as written, so defaults do not apply to an instance that declares anything at all.

stickies._comment: CatBootstrap contributes its OWN card, which is the whole point of the contribution seam: this file cannot import cat-harness, so a code registry would be a seam bootstrap could not reach. ORDER 90 is bootstrap's own judgement that it is the least interesting card on the board — a layer can only state its own priority, it cannot see the others, and without a declared order the board would render in dependency-resolution order (deepest dependency first), putting this above the instance's own description. THEME `bootstrap`, its OWN, per the convention "each harness hould have its own unique theme". It was `pale-sage` — palette-only, no backdrop — for as long as bootstrap had no art of its own, which satisfied the earlier ruling ("i want the grumpy cat moved out of bootstrap and into cat harness") by having no cat at all. The owner supplied art on 2026-09-20, so the ruling is now satisfied the better way: bootstrap has a cat, and it is NOT cat-harness's. NO GH-PAGES LINK: the owner asked for "link back to the source code + ghpaghes for boot strrap", and bootstrap HAS NO SITE. This instance's canonicalUrl is cat-harness's site, not bootstrap's. Declaring a link to a page that does not exist would be a 404 on the landing page; add one line here when the URL exists.  RTFM LINK ADDED on the owner's instruction, 2026-09-20: "all sticky notes should be at end of initiation process for that harnes and provife links to that harness's docs (RTFM=...)". It points at bootstrap's OWN README rather than at this site, because this site is cat-harness's — and it is a github.com blob URL rather than a page URL for the same reason the gh-pages link is still absent: bootstrap has no site of its own yet. Its README is self-documenting on the forge, which the instance declares as an asset, so the link resolves to something that really is bootstrap's documentation.  TEXT BOX declared rather than left to the art's cloud: the measured cloud on the card crop is 0.80 x 0.24, and this card carries a sentence plus two links with notes — it clipped top and bottom at both ends. The box here is the cloud WIDENED DOWNWARD into the lower half of the cloud shape, which is still cloud rather than sky, plus a scale of 0.82. That is the trade the schema exists to make visible: the card says which way it bought the room.  SCOPE LINE added per "also some guidance what is its scope". `bodyAppend` rather than a literal body, so the description above stays the single source of the first sentence.

stickies.bodyAppend: **Scope:** phase one of two, and valid with NOTHING installed — no skills, no knowledge graph, no MCP, no beans. One process lives here and only one. Everything else is composed on top of it, and nothing here may import from the layer above.

directories.description: The two JSON Schema documents the discussion process is checked against — `discussion.input.schema.json` (what is known before asking) and `discussion.output.schema.json` (what the exchange determined). MOVED OUT OF `skills/` on 2026-09-21: a schema is not an instruction body, and while they sat among the `.md` a consumer asking this instance for its schemas was told it has none. This directory was deliberately NOT created when the rest of the layout was split, because declaring a directory that does not exist is the `dh4f` defect — the files had to move first. Their published `$id`s are UNCHANGED and still read `/bootstrap/skills/discussion/`: `gen-bootstrap-schemas.ts` calls that half of a contract cited from five languages' catalogues, and ids are stable across a relocation while paths are not. `graphKinds: ["schemas"]` alone, matching `bootstrap-tools`'s self-declaration of its own `schemas/`; the `["schemas", "cat-harness"]` pairing is how the ROOT declares somebody else's.

CatBootstrap's three Roles — Initiator, Knowledge Graph Data Store, and the person asking. Declared as `scenarios` on 2026-09-21, matching `cat-harness/scenarios/`: before the split this inherited `skills` from the directory above it, so a consumer asking for the Scenarios got skill bodies and a consumer asking for Skills got a role registry. A lane name is a string the audit cannot bind to anything, which is why these Roles were declared at all rather than left implicit in the diagrams' lanes. RENAMED from `bootstrap-roles` on 2026-09-21: `DEFAULT_DIRECTORIES` carries `scenarios` as the convention, and overrides match on ID, so a qualified id did not override the default — it ADDED a second entry at the same path and this directory resolved TWICE. The same defect was fixed in `cat-harness/cat-harness.json` and missed here. The id had to differ from `cat-harness`, which `skills/` holds; `scenarios` was always free.

The bootstrap PROCESSES — `initialize-harness.bpmn`, the one an actor starts, and `log-message.bpmn`, an independent sub-process any step may call. Declared because discovery reads declarations rather than walking the tree: until 2026-09-19 `findBpmnDirs` found this directory by WALKING from the repository root, which also walked it into folio-assistant's graph (88 references to `Process_CatBootstrap` in `_kg/folio-assistant.jsonld`, measured). A separate id from `cat-harness`, because overrides match on id and `skills/` already holds that one — reusing it would replace bootstrap's skills with its workflows. RENAMED from `bootstrap-processes` on 2026-09-21: `DEFAULT_DIRECTORIES` carries `processes` as the convention, and overrides match on ID, so a qualified id did not override the default — it ADDED a second entry at the same path and this directory resolved TWICE. The same defect was fixed in `cat-harness/cat-harness.json` and missed here. The id had to differ from `cat-harness`, which `skills/` holds; `processes` was always free.

The skills for RENDERING this instance's own graph as `.jsonld`/`.json` — `bootstrap-graph-emission` (what the document contains and the four properties it holds) and `bootstrap-graph-publication` (where it lands, why its `@id` must equal that path, and why it is no longer committed). A SEPARATE id from `cat-harness`, which `skills/` already holds: overrides match on id, so reusing it would replace bootstrap's skills with these. SEPARATE from `skills/` as a package too, because the two answer different questions — `skills/` is about READING a graph cold and about the initialization flow, this is about bootstrap EMITTING its own. Until this directory existed the emission discipline lived in a code comment in `kg-export.ts` and a YAML comment in `docs-site.yml`, which is why it was rediscovered rather than read. Bean `hfkl`.

Which languages a model is good at, and whether anybody checked. In BOOTSTRAP for the reason everything else here is: an agent reaching for the language it should communicate in has not yet loaded the harness that would otherwise answer, so a registry one layer up would be unreachable in exactly the case it exists for. `context`: read when a session opens, never written by a process — a person grants a validation, an agent never does, because a model's own claim about its languages is the thing the validation state exists to distrust.

The swimlane glossary's retirement ledger. Declared rather than hidden because a consumer must be able to find what this instance has ever called a term: the glossary document is regenerated from the corpus each run and has no memory, so the one fact that cannot be re-derived — that a concept was once minted — is committed here. Keyed by the IRI's local part, never the absolute IRI, because the publication base is a deploy-time variable and a stored absolute IRI would rot the day it moved.

renderExemption._comment: Owner, 2026-09-20, verbatim: "it is exception to harness/layer not having visualtion/workflow visualizer. but it must have its json/jsonld... that is its existence." Declared here rather than hardcoded in the `2krx` checker, because a checker that names one instance states a rule true only for the instance somebody remembered. `owes` is required by the schema: an exemption with no substitute is a hole, and bootstrap is not dropping out of the requirement — it is trading a criterion it could fail quietly for one it cannot.
renderExemption.reason: bootstrap IS the navbar footer. It is what an agent reads before it knows what this repository is, valid with nothing installed — no skills, no knowledge graph, no MCP, no beans — so it produces nothing a human browses. The requirement is a floor that RISES rather than a flat rule: it starts at cat-harness, which is obliged because it supplies the layers above with `folio/`, and a layer that hands its dependents a folio while rendering nothing itself is asking of them what it did not do.
renderExemption.owes: Its own graph, emitted as `.jsonld` with a `.json` alias and published at `<base>/bootstrap/bootstrap.jsonld` — the exact path its `@id` names. Governed by `render/bootstrap-graph-emission.md` and `render/bootstrap-graph-publication.md`, generated by `cat-harness/scripts/gen-bootstrap-graph.ts`, published by `.github/workflows/docs-site.yml`, and asserted in `cat-harness/scripts/tests/bootstrap-graph.test.ts`.

_needs_comment: The layer this instance sits on. Owner, 2026-09-20: "So bootsteap, cat harness, fa-core, f-a, from bottom to top." Declared rather than hardcoded in the navbar, so the ordering is a fact of the repository and not of whichever consumer needed it first. An EMPTY list is an assertion that this instance sits on nothing — the floor — while an ABSENT one means nobody has said, and the two are different answers.
